clue.text: It's the quickest way to get high, honestly

definitions.text: It's the quickest way to get high
definitions.meaning: going vertically upwards is the shortest route to a height
said truthfully, without evasion, as in telling someone something plainly

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads like drug talk but is literal: rising vertically is the fastest climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both vertically upward and, colloquially, frankly or honestly.

clue.text: So securing a hit needed a bit of brains

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: thus means so
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Grabbing a quick success required some intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a part of the brain, so a bit of brains anatomically.

clue.text: Chief not elected any more?

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: again means once more
in means elected, as a winning party is in

explanation.surface: A leader who no longer holds office wonders about re-election.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a commander or chief official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Some dirt encrusting a silver coin

indicators.note: encrusting means forming a crust around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: grot is slang for dirt or rubbish

explanation.surface: Grime has caked over an old silver piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A GROAT was an old English silver coin worth four pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The groat was a medieval English silver coin worth fourpence.

clue.text: Take steps to press on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take steps' looks like taking action, and 'press on' like carrying on; both are literal footwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily, crushing whatever is underfoot.

clue.text: Cooperate, and put on a record that's acquired new quietly at first

indicators.note: at first places this letter at the very start of the answer

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
to lay is to put on, as in laying a table

indicators.note: something that has acquired another holds it inside

parts.note: a log is a record

explanation.surface: Go along with things and play a newly bought record softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To play along is to go along with something, cooperating.

clue.text: Put Out More Flags

parts.note: the title of an Evelyn Waugh novel, read literally as laying down more flagstones on a path

explanation.walkthrough: Put Out More Flags is an Evelyn Waugh novel; flags here are flagstones, which are laid to surface a path.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying flagstones over ground is surfacing it with paving slabs.

clue.text: How to come to the point of being friendly with a couple of girls picked up

definitions.text: How to come to the point

indicators.note: with here means holding, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pally means friendly

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the pieces read upwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
Mary is a second girl's name

explanation.surface: Advice on getting to the point while being chummy with two girls you met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns DIMARY into YRAMID, which goes inside PALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid narrows to an apex, so tapering pyramidally is coming to a point.

clue.text: Archdeacon subject to delay, it's implied, in Italian city

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is an archdeacon's title
put on ice means postponed, so ice is implied

explanation.surface: A churchman is held up in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: To put something on ice is to postpone it, hence 'it's implied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is a city in north-east Italy.

clue.text: It looks like something may be thrown in this section

definitions.text: It looks like something may be thrown in this section

parts.words: It looks like something may be thrown in this section
parts.note: describes the curved path of a thrown object, and section hints at a conic section in geometry

explanation.walkthrough: A thrown ball follows this curve, and it is one of the conic sections, which explains 'section'.
explanation.definitionFit: The curve is the shape of a projectile's flight and is a conic section.

clue.text: Complete rights retained by a worker

indicators.note: something retained by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
R is the abbreviation for right, so two make RR

explanation.surface: A labourer keeps hold of all his entitlements.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter or out-and-out, as in an arrant fool, so complete in an intensifying sense.

clue.text: Be sure to accommodate request it contains

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: 'you bet' means be sure, so bet stands for being sure
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make certain a request is fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is at the end: a container is defined simply as something that holds 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket is a container, something that holds whatever is put in it.

clue.text: Just recognise sir may catch naughty boys drinking whisky

indicators.note: to catch is to grab hold of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a knight is addressed as sir

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: W is whisky in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A gentleman might find unruly lads boozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sir may' suggests a polite request, but sir is the title of a knight; 'naughty', 'drinking' and 'may catch' work in turn, with W slipped in after the first scrambled letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To know someone by sight is to recognise them without being acquainted, merely recognising them.

clue.text: Chemist's quick to limit damage

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it on both sides, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm means damage

explanation.surface: A druggist is swift to contain harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's in British usage is a shop selling medicines, a drugstore.

clue.text: No longer having a problem how to serve traditional real ale?

definitions.meaning: idiom for being clear of difficulty or danger

definitions.text: how to serve traditional real ale?
definitions.meaning: traditional beer is drawn from a wooden cask

explanation.walkthrough: Real ale is traditional British cask beer; drawn from a wooden barrel it comes, punningly, out of the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past danger, and literally describes beer drawn from a wooden cask.

clue.text: Using pull, was boss being very fair?

parts.note: to tow is to pull
headed means led, was in charge

explanation.surface: A manager wonders if using influence was really fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like justice but means pale-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Tow-headed means having very pale, flaxen hair.

clue.text: Go topless and dance about, ignoring last witty remarks

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: ignoring last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a party is a dance or social

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: wee is a childish word for urinate, go

explanation.surface: Someone strips off and dances about, ignoring the latest clever comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty conversation and retorts.

clue.text: Where a strike will be the best option

definitions.text: Where a strike will be the best option

parts.words: Where a strike will be the best option
parts.note: reads like industrial action, but a strike in tenpins knocks down every pin

explanation.walkthrough: A 'strike' sounds like industrial action; in tenpin bowling it means felling all ten pins with one ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenpin bowling is played in this venue, where a strike is the top result.

clue.text: Imagine supporting fashionable minority

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: in means fashionable
to fancy is to imagine

explanation.surface: Picture yourself backing a trendy small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minority' looks like a small group, but its legal sense is being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Minority in its legal sense means being under age, as in early childhood.

clue.text: Nick a couple of packs, before beginning to play

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: in rugby a scrum is formed by the two packs of forwards

indicators.note: beginning picks just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Steal some cards before the game starts.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMP is British slang for stealing fruit from orchards; in rugby a scrum is where the two forward packs meet.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrump is to steal apples from an orchard, so to nick.

clue.text: Chef lies about frozen topping

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook tells untruths about an iced dessert topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHEF LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: This floating sheet of ice tops the sea along polar coasts, a frozen covering.

clue.text: Organic food containing colouring rejected, when popular previously

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: hay is natural fodder for animals

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: dye is a colouring

explanation.surface: Natural produce with artificial colour is spurned, though it was once fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the colouring round before 'containing' wraps the food about it; hay counts as organic food for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heyday is the time of greatest success or popularity, now past.

clue.text: Stay on the air

parts.note: reads like keeping a broadcast going but means staying aloft

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the air' suggests broadcasting, but it means remaining up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to remain suspended in one spot in the air.

clue.text: Enlarged on reviewing excavation routine

indicators.note: reviewing suggests looking back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a dig is an excavation
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: An archaeologist expands on looking back at the daily grind of digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reviewing' turns DIGRUT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgid means swollen or distended, so enlarged by fluid or pressure.

clue.text: Find a way in the front, going back to the first entrance

indicators.note: going back means travelling in reverse, so the word is turned round

parts.note: the van is the front, as in the vanguard
I is the Roman numeral one, the first
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Directions to someone: head in at the front, then go back to the first door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns VAN into NAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plot a route, finding one's way.

clue.text: Room reserved in the Big Apple

indicators.note: reserved means kept inside, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A booked room in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Apple is New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is a space, room left between things.

clue.text: Hints about doing the double, perhaps

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints

explanation.surface: Suggestions about how to win two races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIPS round. 'Doing the double' sounds like a sporting feat, but a double is a lookalike: the dead spit of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit, as in the very spit of someone, means an exact likeness.

clue.text: In smart clothing, I try to diddle tourist

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: dapper means smartly dressed

indicators.note: to diddle is to cheat or fiddle, so the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A well-dressed con artist attempts to swindle a sightseer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to diddle' scrambles I TRY, and 'clothing' wraps the smart word around it, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A day tripper is a visitor making a single-day excursion, a sort of tourist.
